scope: Locator for the narrative movement and geographic framework in chapters I-II, not an inventory of incidental comparison places and not a reconstructed historical itinerary.

geometry.provenance: Subset of existing course public-domain Natural Earth cache. Original cache documentation accessed 2026-09-11. Current boundaries are orientation only. Source geometry preserved; unused properties removed.
Named Niger and Benue features from existing Natural Earth cache. Not equated with chapter II unnamed river.
Barbados feature retrieved 2026-10-28. 1:10m generalized coastline, not cadastral detail.

markers.name: Bridgetown
markers.status: city locator, approximate town-centre coordinate; no claim to locate historical ship anchorage or sale yard
markers.crosscheck: UNESCO Historic Bridgetown/Garrison coordinate 13.096667,-59.613889 lies about 0.5 km away and covers the larger heritage property; https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1376/maps/

markers.name: Benin City
markers.status: historical-kingdom contextual city, not a narrative journey stop

markers.name: Igbo-speaking region
markers.status: broad illustrative regional symbol, not a surveyed ethnic boundary; no village pinned
markers.limitation: Igbo-speaking communities also extend beyond this illustrative region. Eboe is the narrative spelling. The oval is intentionally not a historical administrative polygon.

movement.warning: Endpoints of arrow are layout locations offshore, not ports. No exact coast embarkation coordinate, date, duration, slave ship, inland track, or sailing track is asserted. Barbados dot is geographically located separately.

primary_text.anchors: Guinea from Senegal to Angola; kingdom of Benen/Benin; Eboe and Essaka (long-s OCR appears Effaka); reference to Abyssinia; brooks and springs.
Tinmah and pond/rivulets; unnamed large river and canoes; six or seven months to unnamed sea coast; ship, Atlantic passage, Barbadoes and Bridge Town; sale and separation of captives.

uncertainty.evidence: Paul E. Lovejoy argues Essaka=Usaka in Abia (2024 online; 2025 journal vol.46 no.2, pp.357-379). Earlier identifications include Isseke; birthplace itself is contested. This map does not adjudicate.

uncertainty.status: scholarly reconstruction, excluded as precise markers
uncertainty.evidence: Paul Lovejoy, Equiano’s World, updated 2024-10-24, proposes Tinmah=Utumah and Calabar departure. Chapter II itself does not name Calabar or the large river.

uncertainty.claim: Abyssinia as eastern extent of Benin
uncertainty.evidence: Chapter I repeats this geographic claim; map does not draw such a kingdom. Modern regional positioning and institutional histories of Benin contradict a transcontinental Benin empire.

uncertainty.status: sale scene, not claim Equiano was sold there
uncertainty.evidence: Chapter II describes the sale and family separation; chapter III specifies Equiano was among those not sold in Barbados and then taken to Virginia. Virginia is out of scope.

qa.rendered: PNG from final PDF visually inspected at 1959 x 1268. No text collisions or clipping. Three detail PNGs allow full-resolution viewing.
qa.fonts: Arial and Arial-Bold embedded TrueType; all authored text sans-serif. Smallest text 11 pt on 17 x 11 inch PDF.
qa.geography: Map projection preserves original country/river geometry. Bridgetown southwest Barbados; Benin City west of Niger in Nigeria; Nigeria east of modern Republic of Benin; westward schematic Atlantic movement.
qa.limitations: Static large-format teaching map; scaled-to-letter printing reduces 11 pt labels and is not recommended. Use tabloid landscape or view at full size.

interactive_web.sources: Same Natural Earth country, Barbados and river geometry as the print maps. No live tile dependency.

views.West Africa: Modern regional context, Niger/Benue not identified with the unnamed river

interactive_web.limits: Elliptical Igbo-region symbol is illustrative, not an ethnic or administrative boundary. No village, departure port, anchorage, or slave-market pin. No historical sailing track.
